q: The dark, ominous clouds over the lake convinced the lifeguards to clear the beach early. Which word is closest in meaning to ominous as used in this sentence?
w: The clouds made the lifeguards clear the beach, so they signaled danger. Ominous means threatening, suggesting that something bad is coming.

n.1: Scattered clouds would not usually clear a beach; ominous means threatening.
n.2: Low clouds may come with storms, but ominous is about a threat, not height.
n.3: Speed is a topic fit for storm clouds, but ominous describes a warning of harm, not motion.

q: After the fire, the family lived on a meager supply of donated food for several weeks. Which word means the opposite of meager as used in this sentence?
w: Meager means small in amount or barely enough, so its opposite is plentiful.

n.1: Unexpected describes surprise, not amount; it is unrelated rather than opposite.
n.2: Insufficient is a synonym of meager (too little), not its opposite: the synonym-for-antonym trap.
n.3: Perishable (likely to spoil) describes food, a topic fit, but it is not the opposite of an amount word.

q: Climbing six flights of stairs after knee surgery was an arduous task for Mr. Brooks. Which word means the opposite of arduous as used in this sentence?
w: Arduous means very difficult and tiring, so its opposite is effortless.

n.0: Exhausting is close to a synonym of arduous, not its opposite.
n.2: Lengthy describes duration; it is not the opposite of hard and tiring.
n.3: Climbing after surgery may be risky, but dangerous is a topic fit, not the opposite of difficult.

q: Three days after the fall, the bruise on her shin was still tender when the nurse pressed on it. What is the best definition of the word tender in this sentence?
w: Tender has several senses; pressing on a bruise selects the sense "painful when touched."

n.0: Easy to chew is the food sense (tender meat); the sentence is about a bruise.
n.1: A bruise may be swollen, a topic fit, but tender here means painful when pressed, not swollen.
n.3: Gentle and loving is a real sense of tender (a tender smile), but a bruise that hurts when pressed rules it out.

q: After the inspection, the engineer declared the old footbridge behind the hospital structurally sound. What is the best definition of the word sound in this sentence?
w: "Structurally" selects the adjective sense of sound: solid, healthy and free of damage.

n.1: Loud relates to the noun sense of sound (noise); "structurally sound" is about condition, not noise.
n.2: Width is a topic fit for a bridge, but sound describes condition, not size.
n.3: An inspection checks condition; nothing says the bridge was rebuilt.

q: The lab detected a minute amount of blood in the urine sample sent from the clinic. What is the best definition of the word minute in this sentence?
w: "Amount" selects the adjective minute (my-NOOT): extremely small.

n.0: Lab results are measured, a topic fit, but minute describes size, not how it was measured.
n.1: Sixty seconds is the noun minute (MIN-it); an "amount of blood" needs a size word.
n.3: Easily seen is close to the opposite: a minute amount is tiny and may be hard to see.

q: The pharmacy will issue a replacement inhaler as soon as the insurance approval arrives. What is the best definition of the word issue in this sentence?
w: As a verb with an object (a replacement inhaler), issue means to give out or supply officially.

n.0: Looking into something treats issue as a problem to investigate (the noun sense); here the pharmacy hands over an inhaler.
n.2: Turning down is the opposite outcome; the pharmacy will supply the inhaler once approval arrives.
n.3: Payment is a topic fit with insurance, but issue means to give out, not to bill.

q: New clients must present a photo ID at the front desk before their first visit. What is the best definition of the word present in this sentence?
w: Present (pre-ZENT) with an object such as an ID means to show or offer it for inspection.

n.0: Attending relates to the adjective sense (present = in attendance, PREZ-ent); here present takes an object, the ID.
n.2: Giving as a gift is another verb sense, but clients keep their ID; they only show it.
n.3: Signing is a topic fit at a front desk, but you present an ID by showing it, not signing it.

q: The research team will conduct interviews with forty nursing students next month. What is the best definition of the word conduct in this sentence?
w: Conduct as a verb with an activity (interviews) as its object means to carry out or direct.

n.0: Behavior is the noun sense (good conduct); here the team conducts interviews, an activity.
n.1: Scheduling is a topic fit, but conducting interviews means actually doing them.
n.2: Transmit is the science sense (copper conducts electricity); interviews are not transmitted.

q: Every shift, the nurse checks the skin integrity on the patient's heels and lower back. What is the best definition of the word integrity in this sentence?
w: With skin, integrity means the state of being whole and unbroken.

n.0: A nurse may note skin color, a topic fit, but integrity means intact and unbroken.
n.1: Honesty is the character sense of integrity; skin cannot be honest, so the sentence rules it out.
n.3: Skin temperature is another check, but it is not what integrity means.

q: The dietitian suggested more legumes, such as lentils, chickpeas and black beans, for fiber and protein. Based on the context, what are legumes?
w: "Such as" introduces an example clue: lentils, chickpeas and black beans are all beans and peas (legumes).

n.0: Leafy greens (spinach, kale) are not in the list of examples.
n.2: Whole grains also give fiber, a topic fit, but the examples are beans and peas, not grains.
n.3: Root vegetables (carrots, beets) grow underground; none is among the examples.

q: The nurse charted bradycardia after counting the patient's pulse at the start of morning rounds. Based on its prefix, what does bradycardia mean?
w: brady- means slow and cardi/o means heart, so bradycardia is a slow heart rate.

n.1: Neither brady- nor cardia refers to rhythm; an irregular rhythm is an arrhythmia.
n.2: A fast heart rate is tachycardia; tachy- means fast, the opposite of brady-.
n.3: Pain would come from a suffix such as -algia or -dynia; brady- describes speed, not pain.

q: A finger-stick test before lunch confirmed hypoglycemia in a patient with type 1 diabetes. Based on its word parts, what does hypoglycemia mean?
w: hypo- means below or deficient, glyc/o means sugar, and -emia means a blood condition, so hypoglycemia is low blood sugar.

n.0: Sugar in the urine would use -uria (urine condition), not -emia (blood condition).
n.2: High blood sugar is hyperglycemia; hyper- (excessive) is the opposite of hypo-.
n.3: The root glyc/o means sugar, not pressure; low blood pressure is hypotension.

q: The patient described a sharp intercostal pain that worsened each time she took a deep breath. Based on its prefix, where is the pain?
w: inter- means between and cost/o means rib, so intercostal pain is felt between the ribs.

n.0: Around is peri- or circum-, not inter-.
n.1: Below the ribs is subcostal (sub- = under).
n.3: Within is intra-, the look-alike prefix; inter- means between.

q: A community clinic posts a flyer for free antenatal classes on Tuesday evenings. Based on its prefix, when are the classes meant to help parents?
w: ante- means before and natal refers to birth, so antenatal classes are for the period before the baby is born (the same meaning as prenatal).

n.1: ante- means before, not during; during would use intra-.
n.2: After birth would be postnatal; post- means after.
n.3: The newborn period is neonatal (neo- = new), not antenatal.

q: A runner who collapsed near the finish line was treated in the medical tent for hyperthermia. Based on its word parts, what does hyperthermia mean?
w: hyper- means above or excessive and therm means heat, so hyperthermia is an abnormally high body temperature.

n.0: Abnormally low body heat is hypothermia; hypo- means below.
n.1: Loss of body water is dehydration (hydr = water); the root here is therm (heat).
n.3: Excessive sweating (hyperhidrosis) shares the prefix hyper-, but the root therm means heat, not sweat.

q: The patient pointed to her epigastric area when she described a burning pain after large meals. Based on its prefix, where is this area?
w: epi- means upon or over and gastr/o means stomach, so the epigastric area lies over the stomach (the upper middle abdomen).

n.1: Behind is retro-, as in retroperitoneal.
n.2: Within is endo- or intra-; epi- means upon or over.
n.3: Below is hypo- or sub- (the hypogastric area lies below the stomach).

q: Before discharge, the nurse reviewed the postoperative care instructions with the patient's family. Based on the prefix, when are these instructions meant to be followed?
w: post- means after, so postoperative care is the care given after an operation.

n.0: Before surgery is preoperative; pre- means before.
n.1: Between is the meaning of inter-, not post-.
n.2: During surgery is intraoperative; intra- means within.

q: A lab report described the patient's red blood cells as macrocytic. Using both the prefix and the root, what does macrocytic describe?
o: Cells that are smaller than normal
Cells that are larger than normal
w: Step 1: macro- means large. Step 2: cyt/o means cell. Macrocytic therefore describes cells that are larger than normal.

n.0: Smaller than normal would be microcytic; micro- means small, the opposite of macro-.
n.1: macro- refers to size, not number; many is multi- or poly-.
n.3: A shortage of cells would use the suffix -penia (deficiency), not macro-.

q: After a stroke, a patient with hemiplegia began working with a physical therapist three times a week. Based on its word parts, what does hemiplegia mean?
o: Paralysis affecting both of the legs
Paralysis on one side of the body
Paralysis of all four of the limbs
Paralysis caused by a brain bleed
w: hemi- means half and -plegia means paralysis, so hemiplegia is paralysis of one half (one side) of the body.

n.0: Paralysis of both legs is paraplegia; hemi- refers to one side, not both legs.
n.2: Paralysis of all four limbs is quadriplegia; quadri- means four.
n.3: hemi- (half) is not hem/o (blood); the word says nothing about bleeding.

q: After the patient's hip surgery, the doctor prescribed an anticoagulant to take for several weeks. Based on the prefix, what does an anticoagulant do?
w: anti- means against, and coagulant refers to clotting, so an anticoagulant works against the clotting of blood.

n.0: anti- does mean against, but the root coagul refers to clotting, not infection (an anti-infective works against infection).
n.1: Speeding up clotting is the opposite of anti- (against).
n.3: Breaking down would be shown by -lysis (as in thrombolysis), not by anti-.

q: A warning label on a can of cleaning solvent reads, "Inflammable: store away from heat, sparks, and open flames." Based on the context, what does inflammable mean?
w: Here in- does not mean not: inflammable means the same as flammable. The context (keep it away from heat, sparks and flames) confirms that the product catches fire easily.

n.0: This also reads in- as "not," which contradicts the instruction to store it away from heat.
n.1: This reads in- as "not," but the warning to keep the can away from flames shows it can catch fire.
n.2: The label's warning is about fire, and nothing in the word parts refers to breathing.

q: The hospital funded a retrospective study of screening outcomes at its three community clinics. Based on its word parts, what does retrospective mean?
w: retro- means backward and spect means look, so retrospective means looking back at past events.

n.0: Within is intra- or endo-, not retro-.
n.2: Looking ahead is the meaning of pro- or pre- words such as prospective; retro- means backward.
n.3: Across is trans-, not retro-.

q: Before the clinical trial began, researchers sorted the volunteers into groups so that each group was homogeneous in age. Based on its prefix, what does homogeneous mean here?
w: homo-/homeo- means same or similar, so a group homogeneous in age is made of people of similar ages.

n.0: Different is hetero- (heterogeneous), the opposite prefix.
n.1: Many is multi- or poly-, not homo-.
n.2: Half is hemi- or semi-, not homo-.

q: During a dressing change, the nurse documented a malodorous discharge from the patient's wound and notified the provider. Based on its prefix, what does malodorous mean?
w: mal- means bad, and odor means smell, so malodorous means having a bad smell.

n.0: No smell would use a- or an- (without), not mal-.
n.1: Faint (less than normal) would match hypo-, not mal-.
n.3: A pleasant smell is the opposite of mal- (bad); good would be eu- or bene.

q: During the resident's quarterly medication review, the geriatric care team flagged polypharmacy as a risk for falls. Based on its word parts, what is polypharmacy?
o: Use of several pharmacies to fill orders
Use of a drug that affects many organs
Use of many medications at the same time
Use of one medication at too high a dose
w: poly- means many and pharmac/o refers to drugs, so polypharmacy is the use of many medications at the same time, which raises the risk of side effects, drug interactions and falls in older adults.

n.0: Here pharmacy refers to drugs (pharmac/o), not to the stores that fill prescriptions; polypharmacy is about how many medications a person takes.
n.1: poly- (many) applies to the drugs themselves; nothing in the word refers to organs or body systems.
n.3: poly- means many, so the word refers to the number of drugs, not to one drug at too high a dose (one is mono- or uni-).

q: A patient with repeated attacks of pain from gallstones is scheduled for a cholecystectomy next week. Using all of its word parts, what will the surgeon do?
w: Step 1: chol/e means bile and cyst/o means bladder or sac, so cholecyst is the bile sac (gallbladder). Step 2: -ectomy means surgical removal. A cholecystectomy removes the gallbladder.

n.0: Visual examination is -scopy, not -ectomy.
n.2: cyst/o alone can mean the urinary bladder, but chol/e (bile) makes this the gallbladder.
n.3: Cutting into an organ is -otomy, not -ectomy.

q: After his bowel surgery, Mr. Grant met with a wound-care nurse to learn how to care for his new colostomy at home. Based on the suffix, what is a colostomy?
o: A surgical incision made into the colon
Surgical removal of part of the colon
Surgical repair of a damaged colon
A surgical opening made for the colon
w: -ostomy means a surgically created opening (a new mouth), so a colostomy is an opening that lets the colon empty through the abdominal wall.

n.0: A cut into an organ is -otomy (colotomy); -ostomy names a created opening, not a simple incision.
n.1: Removal is -ectomy (colectomy).
n.2: Repair is -plasty.

q: Before the next patient's procedure, the technician cleaned and tested the endoscope according to the hospital's infection-control policy. Based on its suffix, what is an endoscope?
o: A record of images from inside the body
A surgical cut made into the body
A procedure that views inside the body
An instrument for viewing inside the body
w: endo- means within and -scope means an instrument for viewing, so an endoscope is the instrument used to look inside the body.

n.0: A record or image is -gram; -scope is the viewing instrument.
n.1: A surgical cut is -otomy; nothing in endoscope refers to cutting.
n.2: The procedure is endoscopy; -scopy names the examination, while -scope names the instrument.

q: After the test, the technician handed the cardiologist a printed tracing that recorded the electrical activity of the patient's heart. Based on its suffix, what is this printed tracing called?
w: Step 1: the item is the record itself, not the process or the machine. Step 2: -gram means a record, so the printed tracing is an electrocardiogram.

n.0: -graph names the instrument that does the recording, not its output.
n.1: -graphy names the process of recording, not the printed record.
n.2: -logy means the study of, a field of knowledge, not a record.

q: During chemotherapy, a patient's blood test revealed leukopenia, so the nurse reviewed infection precautions with him. Based on its word parts, what does leukopenia mean?
o: A deficiency of white blood cells
A cancer of the white blood cells
An excess of white blood cells
A deficiency of red blood cells
w: leuk/o means white and -penia means deficiency, so leukopenia is a shortage of white blood cells (which explains the infection precautions).

n.1: Cancer would be shown by carcin/o or -oma (or -emia in leukemia, a blood condition); -penia means deficiency.
n.2: An excess would use hyper- or -cytosis; -penia means deficiency.
n.3: Red is erythr/o; leuk/o means white.

q: A chest X-ray and an echocardiogram both showed cardiomegaly in a patient with long-term high blood pressure. Based on its word parts, what does cardiomegaly mean?
w: cardi/o means heart and -megaly means enlargement, so cardiomegaly is an enlarged heart.

n.0: Hardening is -sclerosis.
n.1: Narrowing is -stenosis (as in aortic stenosis).
n.3: Softening is -malacia.

q: The provider explained to an older patient that her bone pain was caused by osteomalacia linked to low vitamin D levels. Based on its word parts, what does osteomalacia mean?
w: oste/o means bone and -malacia means softening, so osteomalacia is softening of the bones.

n.0: Inflammation is -itis (osteitis).
n.2: Hardening is -sclerosis, not -malacia.
n.3: Cartilage is chondr/o (chondromalacia); oste/o means bone.

q: The lab returned the patient's sample with a note that hemolysis had occurred during collection, so the blood had to be drawn again. Based on its word parts, what does hemolysis mean?
w: hem/o means blood and -lysis means breakdown or destruction, so hemolysis is the breakdown of (red) blood cells.

n.0: Bursting forth of blood (bleeding) is hemorrhage; -rrhage is the suffix.
n.2: A clot is thromb/o (thrombosis); -lysis means breakdown, the opposite of forming a clot.
n.3: Stopping blood flow is hemostasis; -stasis means stopping.

q: After a long flight, a patient developed pain and redness in her calf, and an ultrasound confirmed thrombophlebitis. Using all of its word parts, what does thrombophlebitis mean?
o: Vein hardening caused by a blood clot
Surgical removal of a clot in a vein
Vein inflammation with a blood clot
Artery inflammation with a blood clot
w: Step 1: thromb/o means clot and phleb/o means vein. Step 2: -itis means inflammation. Together: inflammation of a vein associated with a blood clot.

n.0: Hardening is -sclerosis; -itis means inflammation.
n.1: Removal is -ectomy (thrombectomy); -itis means inflammation.
n.3: Artery is arteri/o; phleb/o means vein.

q: A mother brings her toddler to the clinic with a mild cold, a low fever, and persistent rhinorrhea. Based on its word parts, what is rhinorrhea?
w: rhin/o means nose and -rrhea means flow or discharge, so rhinorrhea is a runny nose.

n.0: Inflammation of the nose is rhinitis (-itis).
n.2: Bleeding (bursting forth) is -rrhage or -rrhagia, the look-alike suffix.
n.3: Surgical repair is -plasty (rhinoplasty).

q: The committee was persuaded by the epidemiologist's credible account of how the outbreak began in a school cafeteria. Based on its root, what does credible mean?
w: The root cred means believe, and -ible means able to be, so credible means believable.

n.0: Hearing is the meaning of aud, as in audible.
n.2: Seeing is the meaning of vis/vid, as in visualize and visible.
n.3: Recognizing (knowing) is the meaning of cogn, as in recognize and cognitive.

q: The physician told the unit clerk that she would dictate her notes on each patient after morning rounds. Based on its root, what will the physician do with her notes?
o: Send them on to another office
w: The root dict means say, so to dictate is to say words aloud for someone (or a device) to record.

n.0: Looking is the meaning of spec/spect (as in inspect).
n.2: Sending is the meaning of mit/mis (as in transmit).
n.3: Writing is the meaning of scrib/script (as in prescription).

q: After the patient's femur fracture, the orthopedic team placed his leg in traction until surgery could be scheduled. Based on its root, what does traction apply to the leg?
o: A twisting force that turns the limb
A steady pulling force on the limb
A brace that carries the limb's weight
A cut that opens the limb's tissue
w: The root tract means pull, so traction is a steady pulling force (used to align a broken bone).

n.0: Turning is the meaning of vert/vers, not tract.
n.2: Carrying is the meaning of port, not tract.
n.3: Cutting is the meaning of sect (as in dissect), not tract.

q: To track her new walking program, an adult patient agreed to wear a pedometer on her waistband all week. Based on its word parts and the context, what does a pedometer most likely measure?
w: ped can mean foot or child, and the context (an adult's walking program) points to foot. A -meter measures, so a pedometer counts steps taken on foot.

n.1: Heart rate would involve cardi/o (heart), which is not in the word.
n.2: Body heat would involve therm (heat), as in thermometer.
n.3: ped can mean child, but the patient is an adult tracking her walking, so foot is the meaning here.

q: Read the sentence: "Before each procedure, staff must ______ every instrument that will touch the patient." Based on its suffix, which word correctly completes the sentence?
w: The blank follows the helping verb must, so it needs a verb. The suffix -ize forms verbs meaning to make, so sterilize (to make sterile) fits.

n.0: Sterile is an adjective; "must sterile every instrument" has no verb.
n.2: -ity forms a noun (the state of being sterile), which cannot follow must.
n.3: -ly forms an adverb, which describes a verb rather than serving as one.

q: The nurse expected the patient's headache to abate within an hour of taking the medication. What is the best definition of the word abate in this sentence?
w: Abate means to become less intense; to subside.

n.1: This is the opposite of abate (escalate or intensify).
n.2: Coming back again is recur; abate means to die down.
n.3: Spreading describes where pain goes, a topic fit; abate is about how strong it is.

q: The dietitian suggested a protein shake to augment the small meals the patient was able to eat. What is the best definition of the word augment in this sentence?
w: Augment means to increase or add to; the shake adds protein to the small meals.

n.0: Digestion is a topic fit for food, but augment means to add to, not to break down.
n.1: Taking the place of is supplant (replace); the shake is added to the meals, not swapped for them.
n.3: Making smaller is diminish, the opposite of augment.

q: The family was told that the patient's kidney function would likely deteriorate over the next several years. What is the best definition of the word deteriorate in this sentence?
w: Deteriorate means to become worse.

n.0: Kidney function may be monitored, a topic fit, but deteriorate describes the change itself.
n.2: Holding steady (stabilize) means no change; deteriorate means a decline.
n.3: Improving is ameliorate, the opposite of deteriorate.

q: The hospital installed brighter hallway lights to enhance safety for patients walking at night. What is the best definition of the word enhance in this sentence?
w: Enhance means to improve the quality or value of something; brighter lights make walking safer.

n.0: Endanger is a look-alike (en- verb) with the opposite effect: it puts at risk.
n.1: Inspecting checks safety; it does not raise it, and it is not what enhance means.
n.3: Publicizing makes something known, a topic fit for a hospital program, not the meaning of enhance.

q: Her blood sugar readings tended to fluctuate when she skipped breakfast and ate late at night. What is the best definition of the word fluctuate in this sentence?
w: Fluctuate means to rise and fall irregularly.

n.0: A steady climb moves in one direction; fluctuate means moving up and down.
n.2: A sharp drop is one movement in one direction; fluctuate means irregular rises and falls.
n.3: Staying steady is the opposite of fluctuate (stabilize).

q: Staff are trained to calm an argument in the waiting room before it can escalate. What is the best definition of the word escalate in this sentence?
w: Escalate means to increase rapidly or become more intense.

n.1: Dying down is de-escalate, the opposite.
n.2: Beginning again is recur or restart; escalate means getting worse.
n.3: Reporting is a topic fit for a waiting-room incident, but escalate means to intensify.

q: Over the long winter, the food bank's supply of canned vegetables began to dwindle. What is the best definition of the word dwindle in this sentence?
w: Dwindle means to become gradually smaller in amount.

n.0: Running out is about amount, a near miss, but dwindle means shrinking gradually, not all at once.
n.2: Growing is the opposite of dwindle.
n.3: Spoiling is a topic fit for food, but dwindle is about amount, not freshness.

q: Without regular cleaning, bacteria can proliferate on the surface of a wooden cutting board. What is the best definition of the word proliferate in this sentence?
w: Proliferate means to increase rapidly in number.

n.1: Resistance to cleaning is a topic fit for bacteria, but proliferate means to multiply rapidly, not to survive cleaners.
n.2: Dying off is the opposite of proliferate.
n.3: Large colonies may become visible, a topic fit, but proliferate means to multiply.

q: The clinic manager called the lab to expedite the test results for the patient in severe pain. What is the best definition of the word expedite in this sentence?
w: Expedite means to make something happen sooner or faster.

n.0: Explaining results is a topic fit, but expedite is about speed.
n.1: Holding up is impede, the opposite of expedite.
n.2: Double-checking is a topic fit for lab results, but expedite means to hurry them.

q: The cream contains an ingredient that may inhibit the growth of new hair on treated skin. What is the best definition of the word inhibit in this sentence?
w: Inhibit means to hold back or restrain; the ingredient slows hair growth.

n.0: Revealing or showing is exhibit, another look-alike.
n.1: Living in is inhabit, the look-alike word.
n.3: Speeding up is the opposite of inhibit (stimulate).

q: Heavy sweating during a long shift can deplete the body's supply of sodium and potassium. What is the best definition of the word deplete in this sentence?
w: Deplete means to use up or reduce the supply of something.

n.1: Protecting the supply is the opposite effect of sweating; deplete means to reduce it.
n.2: Refilling is replenish, the opposite of deplete.
n.3: Measuring is a topic fit for electrolyte levels, but deplete means to use up.

q: The surgeon told Mr. Ortiz that the risk of infection from the procedure was negligible. What is the best definition of the word negligible in this sentence?
w: Negligible means so small that it is unimportant.

n.0: Large and noticeable is the opposite (substantial).
n.1: Speed of onset is a topic fit for infection, but negligible is about size, not timing.
n.3: Caused by carelessness is the meaning of the look-alike negligent.

q: The patient with a chest cold coughed up copious amounts of thick mucus through the night. What is the best definition of the word copious in this sentence?
w: Copious means large in quantity; plentiful.

n.0: Coughing may hurt, but copious describes the amount of mucus, not pain.
n.1: Mucus may be discolored, a topic fit, but copious describes amount, not color.
n.2: Scant is the opposite of copious.

q: When one kidney is removed, the other kidney often grows larger to compensate for the loss. What is the best definition of the word compensate in this sentence?
w: Compensate (for) means to make up for a loss or lack.

n.0: Accounting for something means explaining it; the kidney grows to replace lost function, not to explain it.
n.1: Suffering from a loss is a topic fit, but the kidney's growth offsets the loss.
n.2: Preparing comes before an event; compensate responds to a loss that has already happened.

q: Testing showed a mild hearing deficit in her left ear after the ear infection cleared. What is the best definition of the word deficit in this sentence?
w: A deficit is a shortfall: an amount by which something is too small. A hearing deficit is a hearing loss.

n.0: Pain is a topic fit after an ear infection, but deficit names a lack, not a sensation.
n.1: Excess or surplus is the opposite of deficit.
n.2: Ringing (tinnitus) is a topic fit for an ear problem, but deficit means a shortfall.

q: Mr. Lee was averse to swallowing pills, so the provider prescribed the drug as a liquid. What is the best definition of the word averse in this sentence?
w: Averse means strongly unwilling or disliking; the provider respected his dislike of pills.

n.0: An allergy is a topic fit for a drug change, but averse is about dislike, not a reaction.
n.1: Being unable is a topic fit, but averse describes unwillingness, not inability.
n.2: Harmful or unfavorable is the meaning of the sound-alike adverse.

q: The benevolent donor paid for the new pediatric wing without asking for her name on it. What is the best definition of the word benevolent in this sentence?
w: Benevolent means kind and wanting to do good.

n.0: A large donor may be rich, a topic fit, but benevolent describes kindness, not wealth.
n.1: Declining credit may suggest modesty, but benevolent means kind and well-meaning.
n.3: Wishing harm is malevolent, the opposite.

q: A diligent student, Rosa reviewed her anatomy flashcards every night for three months. What is the best definition of the word diligent in this sentence?
w: Diligent means careful and hardworking.

n.0: Nightly study could come from worry, but diligent means steady and hardworking.
n.1: Natural talent is a topic fit for a good student, but diligent describes effort, not ability.
n.3: Distracted is the opposite of diligent.

q: The pharmacist was meticulous in checking each label against the order before filling it. What is the best definition of the word meticulous in this sentence?
w: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail.

n.0: Following rules is a topic fit for a pharmacist, but meticulous describes attention to detail.
n.1: Nervousness may make someone recheck, but meticulous names the careful habit, not the feeling.
n.2: Speed is a different quality; meticulous is about care with details, not quickness.

q: After years without an accident, the roofing crew grew complacent about checking their harnesses. What is the best definition of the word complacent in this sentence?
w: Complacent means self-satisfied and unaware of possible danger.

n.0: Eager to please is complaisant, another look-alike.
n.1: Willing to obey is compliant, a look-alike with nearly the opposite effect.
n.3: Fatigue could cause lapses, a topic fit, but complacent means smug, not tired.

q: The resilient teenager returned to her soccer team only months after major knee surgery. What is the best definition of the word resilient in this sentence?
w: Resilient means able to recover quickly from difficulty.

n.0: Resisting change is resistant, a look-alike.
n.2: Reluctant (unwilling) is a look-alike with the opposite sense here.
n.3: Eagerness to play is a topic fit for an athlete, but resilient means able to recover quickly, not keen to compete.

q: Despite three failed attempts, the tenacious applicant studied all summer and passed the exam in August. What is the best definition of the word tenacious in this sentence?
w: Tenacious means holding firmly; persistent.

n.0: Weak or flimsy is the meaning of the look-alike tenuous.
n.2: Dull and tiresome is the meaning of tedious.
n.3: Worry is a topic fit for failed attempts, but tenacious means determined.

q: The teenager seemed indifferent to the nurse's warnings about vaping and kept scrolling on his phone. What is the best definition of the word indifferent in this sentence?
w: Indifferent means having no particular interest or concern.

n.1: Hostility would show anger; scrolling on his phone shows lack of interest, not aggression.
n.2: Fear is the reaction the warnings aimed for; indifferent is the lack of any reaction.
n.3: Confusion is a topic fit for a warning, but indifferent means not caring.

q: Lena was ambivalent about moving her mother into an assisted living facility near her home. What is the best definition of the word ambivalent in this sentence?
w: Ambivalent means having mixed or contradictory feelings about something.

n.1: Having firmly decided (adamant) is the opposite of ambivalent.
n.2: Having no strong opinion is indifferent; ambivalent means strong feelings pulling both ways.
n.3: An unclear meaning is ambiguous, the look-alike word.

q: The nurse was discreet when asking about the patient's finances, speaking quietly behind a closed curtain. What is the best definition of the word discreet in this sentence?
w: Discreet means careful to keep things private; tactful.

n.0: Asking about finances is a topic fit for nosiness, but discreet describes how carefully she asked.
n.2: Separate and distinct is discrete, the sound-alike spelling.
n.3: Blunt and direct is the opposite of discreet.

q: Jordan made an impulsive decision to quit his job the same afternoon his manager criticized him. What is the best definition of the word impulsive in this sentence?
w: Impulsive means acting suddenly without careful thought.

n.0: Carefully planned is the opposite of impulsive.
n.1: Showing no emotion is impassive, a look-alike.
n.2: Being forced by others would not make a choice impulsive; compulsive describes an irresistible urge.

q: The doctor warned that a sedentary job could raise the risk of heart disease over time. What is the best definition of the word sedentary in this sentence?
w: Sedentary means spending much time seated; physically inactive.

n.1: Physically demanding is close to the opposite: a sedentary job involves little physical activity.
n.2: A fast pace describes how busy the work is; sedentary means the worker sits most of the time.
n.3: Stress also raises heart risk, a topic fit, but sedentary describes inactivity.

q: Parents of toddlers must stay vigilant near swimming pools, even when a lifeguard is on duty. What is the best definition of the word vigilant in this sentence?
w: Vigilant means watchful and alert to danger.

n.0: Calm and relaxed is close to the opposite of staying on guard.
n.2: Strictness is a parenting topic fit, but vigilant means watchful, not harsh.
n.3: Strong and energetic is vigorous, the look-alike.

q: The obstinate patient refused to use his walker, even after falling twice in the hallway. What is the best definition of the word obstinate in this sentence?
w: Obstinate means stubbornly refusing to change.

n.0: Unsteady fits a man who falls, a topic fit, but obstinate describes his attitude.
n.2: Outdated is obsolete, a look-alike.
n.3: Forgetting would not explain refusing after two falls; obstinate means stubborn.

q: It is prudent to keep a written list of your medications in your wallet in case of an emergency. What is the best definition of the word prudent in this sentence?
w: Prudent means careful and wise about the future.

n.0: A paper list may seem old-fashioned, but prudent means sensible.
n.1: Many people may advise keeping a list, a topic fit, but prudent describes the action as wise, not as often recommended.
n.3: Legal requirements are a topic fit for medication rules, but prudent means wise, not mandatory.

q: The charge nurse asked for a concise report at shift change because the unit was short-staffed. What is the best definition of the word concise in this sentence?
w: Concise means brief but complete: all the needed information in few words.

n.0: Long and detailed is the opposite of concise.
n.2: Shift reports are often spoken, a topic fit, but concise is about length.
n.3: Exact and correct is precise, the look-alike.

q: The clinic offers a comprehensive eye exam for new patients on Saturday mornings. What is the best definition of the word comprehensive in this sentence?
w: Comprehensive means including all or nearly all parts; complete.

n.1: Easy to understand is comprehensible, the look-alike.
n.2: Cost is a topic fit for a clinic offer, but comprehensive describes scope.
n.3: Quick and basic is the opposite of comprehensive.

q: Before signing the consent form, Mrs. Diaz asked the surgeon to clarify one of the listed risks. What is the best definition of the word clarify in this sentence?
w: Clarify means to make clearer or easier to understand.

n.0: Sorting into groups is classify, the look-alike.
n.1: Making a risk smaller is reduce, a topic fit; clarify is about understanding.
n.3: Repeating may not make anything clearer; clarify means to explain more clearly.

q: The interviewer asked the nursing applicant to elaborate on her volunteer work at the shelter. What is the best definition of the word elaborate in this sentence?
w: As a verb, elaborate (on) means to add more detail.

n.0: Leaving it out is eliminate; the interviewer wants more, not less.
n.1: Working with others is collaborate, the look-alike.
n.2: Keeping it brief is the opposite of elaborate.

q: From the empty pill bottles on the counter, the home health aide could infer that the patient needed a refill. What is the best definition of the word infer in this sentence?
w: Infer means to reach a conclusion from evidence; the listener or observer infers.

n.0: Postponing is defer, a look-alike.
n.1: Suggesting indirectly is imply; the speaker implies, while the observer infers.
n.3: Informing someone tells them; infer is drawing a conclusion yourself.

q: From the rash and the recent camping trip, the provider was able to deduce the likely cause. What is the best definition of the word deduce in this sentence?
w: Deduce means to reach a conclusion by reasoning.

n.0: Bringing about is induce.
n.2: Subtracting is deduct, the look-alike.
n.3: Lessening is reduce.

q: In the dim light, the nurse could barely discern the numbers printed on the small vial. What is the best definition of the word discern in this sentence?
w: Discern means to notice or recognize, often with difficulty; to make out.

n.1: Throwing away is discard, a look-alike.
n.2: Worrying about something is concern, a look-alike.
n.3: Looking down on someone is disdain, another look-alike.

q: Nurses and pharmacists collaborate to review each patient's medications before discharge. What is the best definition of the word collaborate in this sentence?
w: Collaborate means to work together.

n.0: Competing is the opposite of working together.
n.2: Adding detail is elaborate, another look-alike.
n.3: Confirming with evidence is corroborate, the classic look-alike.

q: Security camera footage helped corroborate the patient's account of how she fell in the parking lot. What is the best definition of the word corroborate in this sentence?
w: Corroborate means to support or confirm with additional evidence.

n.0: Contradicting is the opposite of corroborating.
n.1: Cameras record, a topic fit, but corroborate means the footage supported her account.
n.2: Working together is collaborate, the look-alike.

q: Both specialists concur that surgery is the best option for repairing the torn tendon. What is the best definition of the word concur in this sentence?
w: Concur means to agree.

n.1: Suspecting is a guess, not agreement.
n.2: Insisting is stronger and one-sided; concur means the two share the same view.
n.3: Doubting is close to the opposite of agreeing.

q: The researcher presented new data to refute the claim that the vaccine causes autism. What is the best definition of the word refute in this sentence?
w: Refute means to prove a statement wrong.

n.1: Refusing is refuse, the look-alike; refute uses evidence to disprove.
n.2: Supporting the claim is the opposite of refuting it.
n.3: Restating repeats a claim; refute disproves it.

q: The handwritten order was ambiguous, so the nurse called the provider before giving the drug. What is the best definition of the word ambiguous in this sentence?
w: Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation; unclear in meaning.

n.0: A missing signature is a topic fit for an order, but ambiguous is about meaning.
n.1: Mixed feelings is ambivalent, the look-alike.
n.2: A handwritten order might be hard to read (illegible), a topic fit, but ambiguous means its meaning is unclear.

q: The discharge sheet gave explicit instructions about when to remove the bandage and shower. What is the best definition of the word explicit in this sentence?
w: Explicit means stated clearly and in detail.

n.0: Forbidden is illicit, a look-alike.
n.2: Instructions can be easy to forget, a topic fit, but explicit means clearly stated.
n.3: Suggested indirectly is implicit, the opposite.

q: Please bring any pertinent medical records, such as recent X-rays, to your first appointment. What is the best definition of the word pertinent in this sentence?
w: Pertinent means relevant to the matter at hand; the X-rays are an example of relevant records.

n.0: Permanent is a look-alike in sound, meaning lasting.
n.1: Rude is impertinent, the look-alike with the prefix im-.
n.2: Original copies are a topic fit for records, but pertinent means relevant.

q: The instructor asked each student to explain the rationale for choosing a particular care plan. What is the best definition of the word rationale in this sentence?
w: Rationale (a noun) means the reasons that explain an action or belief.

n.0: The written steps are the plan itself; the rationale is why it was chosen.
n.1: The result is the outcome, not the reasons behind the choice.
n.2: A fixed share is a ration, a look-alike.

q: The first dose was given in the clinic, and subsequent doses will be taken at home. What is the best definition of the word subsequent in this sentence?
w: Subsequent means coming after something else.

n.1: Dose size is a topic fit, but subsequent is about order in time.
n.2: Whether a dose is optional is a topic fit, but subsequent describes what comes next in time.
n.3: Earlier is the opposite (prior or preceding).

q: The patient is receiving concurrent radiation and chemotherapy during the six-week program. What is the best definition of the word concurrent in this sentence?
w: Concurrent means happening at the same time.

n.0: One after another is consecutive, the classic look-alike.
n.1: Current (up to date) shares letters but means something different.
n.2: Now and then is intermittent or sporadic, not at the same time.

q: She worked three consecutive night shifts and then had four days off. What is the best definition of the word consecutive in this sentence?
w: Consecutive means following one after another without a break.

n.0: Spread out is the opposite of back-to-back.
n.1: At the same time is concurrent, the look-alike.
n.3: Extra shifts are a topic fit, but consecutive describes order, not pay.

q: Sporadic power outages during the storm forced the clinic to switch to its backup generator. What is the best definition of the word sporadic in this sentence?
w: Sporadic means happening at irregular, scattered times.

n.1: Regular intervals is periodic, the look-alike pattern word.
n.2: A storm may affect a wide area, a topic fit, but sporadic describes timing.
n.3: Lasting a long time is prolonged; sporadic describes scattered timing.

q: An interim manager will run the unit until a permanent replacement is hired this spring. What is the best definition of the word interim in this sentence?
w: Interim means serving for the time between two events; temporary.

n.0: Inexperienced suggests intern, a look-alike.
n.1: Part-time describes hours worked; interim describes a limited period of service.
n.2: From inside suggests internal or interior, look-alikes.

q: The preliminary test results were normal, but the final report will take another week. What is the best definition of the word preliminary in this sentence?
w: Preliminary means coming before and preparing for the main part.

n.1: Preventive means stopping something from happening; it does not describe early results.
n.2: Most important is primary, a look-alike.
n.3: Detail is a topic fit for lab results, but preliminary describes results that come first, before the main report, not how detailed they are.

q: With the river still rising, flooding in the lower parking lot seemed inevitable to the hospital staff. What is the best definition of the word inevitable in this sentence?
w: Inevitable means certain to happen; unavoidable.

n.0: Unnoticed describes awareness, not whether the flood will happen.
n.1: Unlikely is close to the opposite.
n.2: Floods are costly, a topic fit, but inevitable describes certainty.

q: The hospital replaced its obsolete paging system with smartphones for every nurse on the unit. What is the best definition of the word obsolete in this sentence?
w: Obsolete means no longer used; out of date.

n.1: Cost is a topic fit for replacing equipment, but obsolete means outdated.
n.2: An old system may fail, but obsolete means replaced by newer technology, not unreliable.
n.3: Noise is a possible complaint about pagers, but obsolete is about being out of date.

q: The duration of the antibiotic course is ten days, even if symptoms improve sooner. What is the best definition of the word duration in this sentence?
w: Duration means the length of time something lasts.

n.1: How a drug is taken is the route; duration is how long.
n.2: The daily amount is the dose, a topic fit for antibiotics.
n.3: Cost is unrelated to duration.

q: The surgeon said a kidney from the patient's brother was a viable option for transplant. What is the best definition of the word viable in this sentence?
w: Viable means capable of working successfully; workable.

n.0: Essential is vital, a look-alike; viable means it can work, not that it is necessary.
n.2: Visible is a look-alike meaning able to be seen.
n.3: Changeable is variable, a look-alike.

q: After the fall, X-rays showed that the patient's hip was intact despite the heavy bruising. What is the best definition of the word intact in this sentence?
w: Intact means whole and undamaged.

n.0: Pain is a topic fit, but an intact hip can still hurt; intact means undamaged.
n.1: Dislocated means out of place, the opposite of intact.
n.3: Swelling is a topic fit after a fall, but intact means not broken.

q: The team decided that home dialysis was feasible because the patient had a willing caregiver. What is the best definition of the word feasible in this sentence?
w: Feasible means possible to do; practical.

n.0: Likely to fail is fallible, a look-alike.
n.1: Easy to bend is flexible, a look-alike.
n.3: Cost is a topic fit, but the caregiver made the plan possible; feasible means workable.

q: Every surgery carries some inherent risk, no matter how skilled the surgeon is. What is the best definition of the word inherent in this sentence?
w: Inherent means existing as a natural, permanent part of something.

n.0: "Some" risk may sound slight, a topic fit, but inherent means built in, not small.
n.1: Avoidable is the opposite; the risk exists no matter how skilled the surgeon.
n.3: Passed down from parents is inherited, the look-alike.

q: A quiet, dark room is conducive to sleep for most patients recovering after surgery. What is the best definition of the word conducive in this sentence?
w: Conducive (to) means making an outcome likely; favorable.

n.0: Harmful is the opposite.
n.1: Carrying heat or electricity is conductive, the look-alike.
n.2: Necessary is too strong: a dark room helps sleep but is not required.

q: The nurse checked that the patient had adequate fluid intake during the hot afternoon. What is the best definition of the word adequate in this sentence?
w: Adequate means enough for a need; satisfactory.

n.0: Excessive means too much, beyond what adequate means.
n.1: Exact is accurate, a look-alike.
n.3: Skillful is adept, a look-alike.
